forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: South Hams Executive agrees £160k rise to £620k budget for leisure centre solar panels
news_drafts.lead:
South Hams District Council is to install solar panels at its Ivybridge, Dartmouth and Totnes leisure centres, with a budget of £620k. The Executive, the council's decision-making committee, agreed a £160k increase to the budget on 16 September. The scheme follows the installation at Kingsbridge.

The £160k increase is financed with £80k from the Climate Change Reserve and £80k from the Business Rates Retention Reserve. Reserves are money the council has put aside. Business rates retention is the share of local business rates the council keeps for itself. The remaining £460k is internal borrowing, which means using the council's own cash reserves to pay for capital spending (money spent on things that last) instead of taking a loan.

The report on capital spending to 31 July 2026 (Appendix A) records no expenditure on the scheme by that date.

news_drafts.headline: South Hams faces £394,000 budget gap for 2027/28 despite identifying £2m in savings
news_drafts.lead: South Hams District Council identified £2.071m in savings and cost reductions for 2027/28 but still faces a shortfall of £394,542, according to its medium-term financial strategy approved at the executive meeting on 16 September. The gap represents 2.6 per cent of the council's projected net budget of £15.152m. Larger deficits are forecast for the following two years: £1.455m in 2028/29 and £1.165m in 2029/30. The council's earmarked reserves are being depleted rapidly to fund capital projects and to cover two major contractor failures — a waste service collapse that cost £4m to bring back in-house, and the administration of leisure contractor Fusion, which required £1.2m to restore services. The council's reserves are projected to fall from £13.957m to £6.731m by March 2028. Government funding cuts have compounded the pressure: the Revenue Support Grant falls from £3.7m to £1.8m over three years, and a business rates reset eliminated £2.5m of income.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A – Details of capital expenditure to 31 July 2026
findings.headline: SH034 statutory EPC improvements to the employment estate show no spend to 31 July 2026 against a £249,000 budget, with the paper saying the project should get back on track once works start on site.
findings.detail: The paper says the LED upgrade budget is on track for spend by year end, but also says the project should be back on track once starting works on site. The budget is funded partly from the Year 2 delivery plan and partly from the climate change funding.
findings.matters: A £249,000 budget with no spend four months into the year, and a comment that delivery depends on works starting, is a timing risk for year-end capital outturn that peer councils will track.
findings.figures: £249,000 total budget; £0 expenditure to 31/07/26; £249,000 2026/27 remaining budget
findings.quote: Project should be back on track once starting works on site.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A – Details of capital expenditure to 31 July 2026
findings.headline: Kingsbridge Pump Track has been built and opened, with £68,211.00 spent to 31 July 2026 against an £80,000 budget.
findings.detail: The tarmac pump track in Kingsbridge Recreation Ground was built in May and June and opened in June. The paper says it is complete apart from a 2.5% retention to be held for 12 months.
findings.matters: A completed project with a retention still held is a small, closed item that shows the council's delivery against a capital bid made in its 2026/27 round.
findings.figures: £80,000 total budget; £68,211.00 spent to 31/07/26; £11,789 remaining; 2.5% retention

findings.paper_title: Appendix A – Details of capital expenditure to 31 July 2026
findings.headline: Totnes Skate Park scheme is complete, with total expenditure of £311,995.12 to 31 March 2026 against a £320,400 approved budget.
findings.detail: The paper records the scheme as complete. Funding is a mix of capital receipts, the Community Reinvestment Fund, Totnes Town Council, fundraising, S106 funds, Crowdfunder and the council plan.
findings.matters: A scheme delivered within its approved budget, with funding drawn from several partners, is an example peer councils can compare against their own project outturns.
findings.figures: £320,400 total approved budget; £311,995.12 spent to 31/03/26; £8,405 remaining budget

findings.paper_title: Appendix A – Details of capital expenditure to 31 July 2026
findings.headline: Capital expenditure to 31 July 2026 is 18.2% of the 2026/27 capital budget, at £1,838,467 against £10,085,573.
findings.detail: The total row, including Appendix B, shows £1,838,467 spent in 2026/27 to 31 July 2026 against a current-year budget of £10,085,573. The paper gives 18.2% as the percentage spend.
findings.matters: A four-month spend rate of 18.2% of the in-year capital budget is a measure finance officers at other councils use to judge whether a programme is on pace.
findings.figures: 18.2%; £1,838,467 spent to 31/07/26; £10,085,573 2026/27 budget; £26,547,356 total capital programme including Appendix B

findings.paper_title: Appendix A – Details of capital expenditure to 31 July 2026
findings.headline: Private sector renewal grants 2025/26 allocation has spent £452,814.62 to 31 July 2026 against a 2026/27 budget of £1,186,414, with the paper citing demand the council does not control.
findings.detail: The paper says spend on Disabled Facilities Grants depends on demand the council has no control over, and that there has been exceptional demand on the budget this year. It also says the policy is being reviewed to allow more flexibility and will go to council.
findings.matters: Demand-led adaptation spend that is running ahead of budget and under a policy review is a pressure that peer councils with statutory DFG duties will recognise.
findings.quote: Spend on DFG’s is based on demand over which the Council has no control
